text: What is the most reliable defining characteristic of cloud computing, according to the Azure AZ-900 module?
options: It is defined strictly by the fact that services travel over the public internet.
It is defined by how the service behaves (delivered on demand, scaling as needed, consumed rather than owned).
It is defined by the elimination of all on-premises hardware.
It is defined by the use of Microsoft proprietary networking technologies.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. The module explicitly states that cloud computing is defined by how the service behaves (on-demand, scalable, consumed) rather than the network it travels over. A, C, and D are wrong because private clouds use internal networks, hybrid clouds retain some on-premises hardware, and cloud is vendor-agnostic.

text: How does the Azure AZ-900 curriculum define the 'Shared Responsibility Model'?
options: The model where the cloud provider manages all physical and logical security.
The model where the customer is completely responsible for all compliance and security.
The division of security and management duties between the cloud provider and the customer.
A pricing model where costs are shared between different tenants.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. The shared responsibility model sets out exactly which security duties transfer to the provider and which stay with the customer. A and B are wrong because responsibilities are explicitly divided, not monopolized. D is wrong because it relates to security/management, not pricing.

text: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure?
options: Building a datacentre
Signing up for a cloud service
Leasing a company vehicle
Renting a convention centre
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Capital expenditure is a one-time, up-front expenditure to purchase or secure tangible resources, and building a datacentre is Microsoft's own example of it. B is wrong because signing up for cloud services is an operational expenditure, paid over time. C is wrong because leasing is payment for use over time, not a purchase. Buying the vehicle would be capital expenditure; leasing it is operational. D is wrong for the same reason. Renting a venue is spending on a service over time.

text: Why does cloud computing fall under operational expenditure rather than capital expenditure?
options: Because cloud services are always cheaper than buying hardware.
Because cloud providers do not allow up-front payments.
Because cloud resources are intangible.
Because cloud computing operates on a consumption-based model, paying for resources used over time.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Cloud computing is classified as operational expenditure precisely because it operates on a consumption-based model, in which you pay for the IT resources you use rather than purchasing infrastructure. A is wrong because cloud computing is not automatically cheaper. It removes wasted capacity, but a badly managed cloud estate can cost more than owned hardware. B is wrong because up-front payment options do exist, for example when purchasing a reservation. The classification does not depend on that. C is wrong because tangibility is not the test. The test is whether the money buys an asset once or pays for a service over time.

text: An organisation running its own datacentre overestimates its future capacity needs. What is the consequence?
options: Applications suffer from decreased performance.
It must order and install more hardware.
Its costs automatically reduce to match actual usage.
It spends more on the datacentre than necessary and potentially wastes money.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Overestimating means paying for capacity that is not fully used, and that money has already been spent. A is wrong because decreased performance is the consequence of underestimating, not overestimating. B is wrong for the same reason. Ordering and installing more hardware, and adding power, cooling and networking for it, is what happens when capacity has been underestimated. C is wrong because automatic cost reduction is a property of the consumption-based model, not of an owned datacentre. Owned hardware costs the same whether it is busy or idle.

text: A student stops a virtual machine at the end of a lab exercise but does not delete it. What is the most accurate description of the billing outcome?
options: All charges associated with the virtual machine stop.
Compute charges stop, but the attached disk continues to be billed as storage.
Charges continue exactly as before.
Charges stop only if the virtual machine is also deallocated from its region.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Stopping a virtual machine stops the compute charge, but the disk holding the operating system continues to exist and continues to be billed. A is wrong, and this is the assumption that produces unexpected bills. Stopping is not the same as deleting. C is wrong because the compute charge, usually the largest component, does stop. D is wrong because deallocation is what stopping a virtual machine achieves. It still leaves the storage in place.

text: Which pricing arrangement involves committing to a specific resource configuration for a one-year or three-year term?
options: Pay-as-you-go
Spot pricing
An Azure reservation
Azure Hybrid Benefit
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A reservation commits you to a specific resource for a fixed term in exchange for a lower rate than pay-as-you-go. A is wrong because pay-as-you-go involves no commitment at all, which is why it carries the highest rate. B is wrong because spot pricing involves no term commitment. It trades reliability for price, not time for price. D is wrong because Azure Hybrid Benefit applies licences you already own. It is not a usage commitment.

text: An organisation has a steady overall level of compute spend, but the specific virtual machine sizes and regions it uses change from quarter to quarter. Which arrangement fits best?
options: Azure savings plan for compute
Azure reservations
Spot pricing
Pay-as-you-go
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. A savings plan commits to an hourly amount of compute spend rather than to a specific resource, and the benefit applies automatically across eligible compute usage, which suits a changing workload mix. B is wrong because a reservation is tied to a specific resource configuration. If the sizes and regions keep changing, the commitment is a poor fit. C is wrong because spot workloads can be evicted at any time, which is unrelated to the steadiness of spend described. D is wrong because the organisation has predictable spend and would be paying the highest rate unnecessarily.

text: Which workload is most appropriate for Azure spot pricing?
options: A public-facing e-commerce website
A company's primary email system
An overnight batch job that can be restarted if interrupted
A database supporting live customer transactions
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Spot pricing offers deep discounts on spare capacity in exchange for accepting that the workload can be evicted, so it suits interruptible work such as batch processing. A is wrong because a public-facing website being switched off without warning would directly affect customers. B is wrong for the same reason. Email is a service users depend on continuously. D is wrong because a database serving live transactions is the least interruptible workload of all.

text: What does Azure Hybrid Benefit allow an organisation to do?
options: Run workloads across Azure and another public cloud provider.
Connect an on-premises datacentre to Azure.
Commit to a fixed hourly compute spend for a discount.
Apply eligible Windows Server or SQL Server licences it already owns to reduce Azure costs.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure Hybrid Benefit lets an organisation apply licences it already holds, so it does not pay a second time for the same software when moving to Azure. The same benefit also covers eligible Red Hat Enterprise Linux and SUSE Linux Enterprise Server subscriptions. A is wrong because using two public providers is multicloud, which is a deployment arrangement rather than a pricing benefit. B is wrong because connecting a datacentre to Azure describes hybrid cloud connectivity, not the licensing benefit. The similar names are the trap in this question. C is wrong because committing to hourly compute spend describes the Azure savings plan for compute.

text: Which statement about serverless computing is correct?
options: No servers are involved in running the code.
Servers are involved, but the customer does not provision or manage them.
The customer must specify how many instances to run.
Serverless applications always cost less than virtual machines.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The code runs on physical hardware in the provider's datacentre. What the term describes is that provisioning, scaling and maintenance are handled by the platform rather than by the customer. A is wrong, and it is the misconception the name creates. Servers absolutely exist. C is wrong because automatic scaling is a defining characteristic of serverless. The platform decides the instance count based on incoming events. D is wrong because for steady, continuous, high-volume workloads a reserved virtual machine is usually cheaper than paying per execution.

text: Which of these is a defining characteristic of serverless computing?
options: Billing is based on a fixed monthly fee regardless of use.
The customer chooses the operating system and patches it.
Billing is based on usage, so no consumption means no charge.
Capacity must be reserved in advance for one or three years.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Serverless is typically billed based on usage, so if no consumption happens, no charges are incurred. This is the purest form of the consumption-based model. A is wrong because a fixed fee regardless of use is the opposite of consumption billing. B is wrong because not managing the operating system is one of the main points of serverless. D is wrong because reserving capacity in advance describes reservations, and it contradicts the elastic scaling that defines serverless.

text: A function application has been idle for several minutes. The first request afterwards takes noticeably longer than usual to respond. What is this called, and why does it happen?
options: Throttling, because the platform limits request rates.
Eviction, because spare capacity was reclaimed.
Latency, because the request travelled to a distant region.
Cold start, because the platform scaled the application down to zero instances and must scale back up.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. When a function application becomes idle, the platform may scale it down to zero instances. The next request carries the added delay of scaling from zero to one, which is called a cold start. A is wrong because throttling limits how many requests are processed, and is a different mechanism entirely. B is wrong because eviction is what happens to a spot virtual machine when Azure reclaims spare capacity. It is not related to serverless idling. C is wrong because regional distance produces a consistent delay on every request, not a delay only on the first request after idleness.

text: An organisation needs to connect several existing business systems together in an automated workflow, without writing code. Which Azure serverless service is designed for this?
options: Azure Logic Apps
Azure Functions
Azure Virtual Machines
Azure Arc
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Azure Logic Apps designs and runs automated, event-driven integration workflows, and provides a large library of prebuilt connectors so services can be joined together without code. B is wrong because Azure Functions is for running your own code. It is the right answer when custom logic is required, and the two services are often used together. C is wrong because virtual machines are infrastructure as a service, which is the opposite of serverless. D is wrong because Azure Arc manages resources hosted outside Azure, as covered in Module 1. It is not a workflow service.

text: An application runs continuously at a high, steady volume, twenty-four hours a day. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Serverless will be cheaper, because it scales automatically.
Serverless will be cheaper, because there is no infrastructure to manage.
A reserved virtual machine is likely to be cheaper, because the workload never idles.
Spot pricing is the correct choice for any steady workload.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Serverless saves money by charging nothing when idle. A workload that never idles cannot benefit from that, so committing to a reserved virtual machine is usually the cheaper arrangement. A is wrong because automatic scaling is valuable for variable demand. Steady demand does not need it. B is wrong because reduced management effort is a real benefit but does not by itself make serverless cheaper at constant high utilisation. D is wrong because spot workloads can be evicted without warning, which is unsuitable for a continuously running production service.

text: An organisation wants its web application to remain reachable even if one datacentre in a region suffers a power failure. Which benefit is being described?
options: Scalability
Agility
Elasticity
High availability
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. The stated goal is to keep the application reachable through a failure, which is the defining purpose of high availability. In Azure it is achieved by spreading instances across availability zones. A is wrong because scalability concerns having enough capacity for the load, not surviving a failure. The scenario says nothing about demand. B is wrong because agility is the speed with which resources can be deployed or changed, which is not what the scenario asks about. C is wrong because elasticity is automatic scaling in response to demand. Again, no change in demand is described.

text: A retailer expects ten times its normal traffic during a sale and adds more identical web servers behind a load balancer. Which type of scaling is this?
options: Vertical scaling
Fault tolerance
Scaling up
Horizontal scaling
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Adding more instances of a resource is horizontal scaling, also called scaling out. The signal is that the number of servers changes while their size does not. A is wrong because vertical scaling changes the size or power of a single instance rather than the number of instances. B is wrong because fault tolerance is the ability to keep operating when a component fails. Extra servers may improve it, but the goal described here is capacity, not survival. C is wrong because scaling up is another name for vertical scaling, so it describes the same thing as option A.

text: A database server is running slowly under complex queries, so it is moved to a larger size with more memory and more processor cores. Which type of scaling is this?
options: Horizontal scaling
Scaling out
Elasticity
Vertical scaling
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Increasing the size or power of an existing instance is vertical scaling, also called scaling up. A is wrong because horizontal scaling changes the number of instances. Only one database server is described. B is wrong because scaling out is another name for horizontal scaling, so it is the same answer as option A. C is wrong because elasticity is automatic adjustment in response to demand. This change was made deliberately in response to a performance problem, not automatically.

text: A service level agreement commits to 99.9 percent uptime. Approximately how much downtime does that permit in a 30-day month?
options: About 4 minutes
About 22 minutes
About 43 minutes
About 7 hours
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Subtracting 99.9 from 100 leaves 0.1 percent. One tenth of one percent of a 30-day month, which contains 43,200 minutes, is about 43 minutes. A is wrong because about 4 minutes a month corresponds to 99.99 percent, which is a far stronger commitment. B is wrong because about 22 minutes a month corresponds to 99.95 percent. D is wrong because about 7 hours a month corresponds to 99 percent. The lesson in this question is that percentages which look almost identical permit wildly different amounts of downtime.

text: Which statement best distinguishes scalability from elasticity?
options: Scalability is the ability to adjust capacity; elasticity is that adjustment happening automatically in response to demand.
Scalability applies to storage and elasticity applies to compute.
Scalability increases capacity and elasticity decreases it.
They are two names for the same property.
Elasticity
Agility
Operational Excellence
Manageability
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Scalability is the capability. Elasticity is the platform exercising that capability automatically, without a person intervening. B is wrong because both terms apply across resource types. The distinction has nothing to do with storage against compute. C is wrong because scalability works in both directions, up and down or out and in, and so does elasticity. D is wrong because the difference is real and is examinable. A system an administrator must scale manually is scalable but not elastic.

text: An organisation can forecast its monthly Azure spending accurately because usage is tracked in real time and billed by consumption. Which benefit does this illustrate?
options: Cost predictability
Performance predictability
Reliability
Governance
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Predictability has two halves, and this scenario describes the cost half: the ability to predict and forecast what the cloud environment will cost. B is wrong because performance predictability concerns predicting the resources needed to deliver a good user experience, not the money. C is wrong because reliability is the ability to recover from failure and continue to function. D is wrong because governance concerns compliance with rules. Cost visibility supports governance but is not what the scenario describes.

text: An administrator uses PowerShell to create resources in Azure. Which aspect of manageability is this?
options: Management of the cloud
Management in the cloud
Governance
Elasticity
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Management in the cloud describes how you interact with the environment, and the four routes are the portal, the command line interface, application programming interfaces and PowerShell. A is wrong because management of the cloud describes what is managed, such as automatic scaling, template-based deployment, health monitoring and alerts. The distinction is of against in. C is wrong because governance concerns rules and compliance rather than the method of interaction. D is wrong because elasticity is automatic scaling in response to demand.

text: Resources are deployed automatically from a preconfigured template, and failing resources are replaced without human intervention. Which aspect of manageability is this?
options: Management in the cloud
High availability
Predictability
Management of the cloud
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Management of the cloud covers what you manage: automatic scaling, deployment from preconfigured templates, monitoring resource health and replacing failing resources, and automatic alerts. A is wrong because management in the cloud is about the interface used, such as the portal or PowerShell. No interface is mentioned here. B is wrong because although replacing failing resources supports availability, the scenario is describing the management capability itself rather than the uptime outcome. C is wrong because predictability concerns confidence about performance and cost.

text: Which statement about Azure Blueprints is currently accurate?
options: It is the recommended service for deploying governed environments in Azure.
It is being retired, with full retirement on 31 January 2027, and Microsoft recommends migrating to Deployment Stacks and template specs.
It has been renamed Azure Policy.
It is generally available and unaffected by any retirement plans.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Azure Blueprints remained in preview and is being retired on 31 January 2027, with a phased withdrawal that began on 31 July 2026. Microsoft recommends Azure Deployment Stacks, with template specs or templates in source control for versioning. A is wrong, and it is what a great deal of current third-party AZ-900 material still says. Treat any guide that presents Blueprints as a current recommendation as dated. C is wrong because Azure Policy is a separate service that continues to exist and is covered in Module 11. Blueprints could apply policies, but the two are not the same thing. D is wrong on both counts. Blueprints never reached general availability, and the retirement is published.

text: A website remains online during a zone failure but responds very slowly because it has too few instances for the traffic it is receiving. Which statement is accurate?
options: The site is neither highly available nor scalable.
The site is highly available but under-scaled.
The site is scalable but not highly available.
The site is elastic.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Remaining online through a zone failure is exactly what high availability provides. Responding slowly because there are too few instances for the load is a shortfall in scalability. The two properties are independent, which is what this question tests. A is wrong because the site demonstrably survived a failure, so it is highly available. C is wrong because it reverses the two. The site survived the failure but lacked capacity, not the other way round. D is wrong because an elastic system would have added capacity automatically as demand rose, which plainly did not happen.

text: An organisation chooses platform as a service so that operating system patching is handled by Microsoft. Which benefit is being exercised?
options: Security, by using the shared responsibility model deliberately
Scalability, because platform services scale automatically
Predictability, because patching happens on a schedule
Agility, because deployment is faster
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. The cloud lets an organisation choose how much of the security work it takes on. Selecting platform as a service so that patching transfers to the provider is the shared responsibility model being used as a deliberate security decision. B is wrong because although platform services do scale well, the scenario states the reason for the choice, and that reason is patching. C is wrong because predictability concerns confidence about performance and cost, not maintenance schedules. D is wrong because although platform services can be quicker to deploy, that is not the stated reason for the choice.

text: Which of the following best describes the governance benefit of cloud computing?
options: The provider secures the physical datacentre.
Resources can be scaled automatically to match demand.
Auditing can flag resources that are out of compliance with corporate standards, and mitigation can be applied automatically.
Costs can be forecast accurately.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Governance concerns whether an environment follows the rules. Cloud auditing can identify non-compliant resources and apply mitigation automatically, which turns a standard into something enforced rather than merely reported. A is wrong because physical datacentre security is the security benefit, delivered through the shared responsibility model. B is wrong because automatic scaling is elasticity. D is wrong because accurate cost forecasting is cost predictability. It supports governance but is not the governance benefit itself.

text: Which service type gives the customer the greatest control over the environment?
options: Software as a service
Platform as a service
Infrastructure as a service
All three give equal control
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Infrastructure as a service provides on-demand access to servers, storage and networks, and the customer manages the operating systems, applications and data. This gives the most control and flexibility of the three. A is wrong because software as a service gives the least control. The application is finished and can only be configured within the options its designers exposed. B is wrong because platform as a service sits between the two. The operating system has already moved to the provider. D is wrong because the three types are three positions on a scale of control, and distinguishing them is the point of the objective.

text: An organisation deploys an application to Azure App Service. Who is responsible for patching the operating system?
options: The organisation
Responsibility is shared equally
No operating system is involved
Microsoft
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure App Service is platform as a service, and the operating system is a Microsoft responsibility at platform as a service and at software as a service. A is wrong because that is the position under infrastructure as a service, where the operating system remains the customer's responsibility. B is wrong because the operating system is not a shared area. Applications and network controls are shared at platform as a service; the operating system belongs wholly to Microsoft. C is wrong because an operating system certainly exists underneath the platform. The point of platform as a service is that it is not your concern, not that it is absent.

text: Which of the following is a Microsoft-published example of infrastructure as a service in Azure?
options: Azure App Service
Microsoft 365
Azure Disk Storage
Azure SQL Database
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft names Azure Virtual Machines, Azure Disk Storage and virtual networks as its infrastructure as a service examples. A is wrong because Azure App Service is named as a platform as a service example. B is wrong because Microsoft 365 is named as a software as a service example. D is wrong because Azure SQL Database is named as a platform as a service example. It is a managed database, so the engine and its maintenance belong to the provider.

text: A company needs to move a fifteen-year-old application to the cloud. The application requires a specific operating system version and particular software installed alongside it, and it cannot be rewritten. Which service type should be used?
options: Infrastructure as a service
Platform as a service
Software as a service
None. The application cannot move to the cloud.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. The scenario states a requirement for a specific operating system configuration and installed software, and only infrastructure as a service gives control of the operating system. This is also the classic lift and shift case. B is wrong because platform as a service removes operating system control, which is precisely what this application requires. C is wrong because software as a service means using a finished application. This organisation has its own application to run. D is wrong because infrastructure as a service exists for exactly this situation. Being unable to rewrite an application is a normal reason to choose it.

text: Which responsibility areas remain wholly with the customer under software as a service?
options: Operating system, applications and network controls
Physical hosts, physical network and physical datacentre
None. The provider takes on everything under software as a service.
Customer data, configurations and settings, and identities and users
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. These are the group one areas from Module 1, and they are Customer at every position on the scale including software as a service. A is wrong because at software as a service the operating system and network controls belong to Microsoft, and applications are shared. B is wrong because the three physical areas belong to Microsoft in all three cloud service types. C is wrong, and it is the most dangerous misconception in this module. Moving to software as a service moves the layers, not the ownership of your data, configuration and identities.

text: A development team wants to build and deploy a web application without provisioning servers or maintaining operating systems. Which service type suits this?
options: Platform as a service
Infrastructure as a service
Software as a service
On-premises
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Platform as a service provides a ready-to-use environment for building, testing and deploying applications, with the provider handling infrastructure and runtime. B is wrong because infrastructure as a service would require the team to provision and maintain servers, which the scenario explicitly rules out. C is wrong because the team is building its own application, not using a finished one. D is wrong because on-premises means owning and managing the entire stack, which is further still from what the scenario asks for.

text: An academy uses Microsoft 365 for staff email and document collaboration. Which service type is this, and what does the academy still remain responsible for?
options: Platform as a service; responsible for the operating system
Software as a service; responsible for nothing
Software as a service; responsible for its data, its configuration and its user identities
Infrastructure as a service; responsible for the servers
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft 365 is a published software as a service example, and the group one responsibilities remain with the customer at every position on the scale. A is wrong on both counts. Microsoft 365 is software as a service, and the operating system belongs to Microsoft at that position. B is wrong because responsible for nothing is never true. Data, configuration and identity never transfer, which is why account compromise remains a customer-side risk in software as a service. D is wrong because no servers are provisioned or managed by the academy.

text: According to Microsoft's published documentation, which service type does Azure Storage belong to?
options: Infrastructure as a service
Platform as a service
Software as a service
It is not a cloud service
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Microsoft lists Azure Storage among its platform as a service examples, alongside Azure App Service, Azure Functions and Azure SQL Database. A is wrong according to Microsoft's documentation, although a great deal of third-party training material makes this claim on the grounds that storage sounds like infrastructure. Note that Azure Disk Storage is a separate service and is listed under infrastructure as a service. C is wrong because Azure Storage is not a finished application that a user signs in to and uses. D is wrong because it is plainly a cloud service. The underlying lesson is that classification depends on how much of the stack you manage, not on what the service is made of.

text: Which statement about the relationship between the three service types is correct?
options: As control increases, management responsibility decreases.
Control and management responsibility are unrelated.
Platform as a service offers both the most control and the least management effort.
As control increases, management responsibility also increases.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. The two move together. Infrastructure as a service offers the most control and requires the most management. Software as a service offers the least control and requires the least management. A is wrong because it reverses the relationship, describing an arrangement that does not exist. B is wrong because the relationship is the central idea of the module. The service types are positions on a single scale. C is wrong because no position offers both. An option claiming maximum control with minimum effort is testing whether you know that.

text: An organisation runs its website on Azure App Service, stores data in Azure SQL Database, runs a legacy reporting tool on an Azure virtual machine, and uses Microsoft 365 for staff email. Which statement is accurate?
options: The organisation is using platform as a service only.
The organisation has made an architectural error by mixing service types.
The organisation is using a combination of service models, which is normal.
The organisation should move everything to infrastructure as a service for consistency.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft states that many Azure solutions use a combination of service models. Choosing the right position on the scale for each workload is what competent architecture looks like. A is wrong because the virtual machine is infrastructure as a service and Microsoft 365 is software as a service. B is wrong because mixing service types is normal and usually correct, not an error. D is wrong because it would move the website and database backwards into a position requiring operating system management for no stated benefit.

text: Which use case is most characteristic of infrastructure as a service?
options: Providing staff with email and collaboration tools
Lift and shift migration of an existing application
Running a managed database where the platform handles patching
Providing a development framework so teams can start with application code
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Lift and shift means moving an existing application to the cloud with little or no change, and it requires an environment that behaves like the server the application already expects. A is wrong because email and collaboration are the classic software as a service use case. Ready-made applications already exist for universal needs. C is wrong because a managed database with platform-handled patching is platform as a service. D is wrong because a development framework that lets teams start with application code is platform as a service.

text: Under platform as a service, applications and network controls are listed as shared responsibilities. What does shared mean in this context?
options: Both parties hold duties in that area, and the customer's duties still require attention.
The responsibility is divided exactly in half.
Either party may choose to take the responsibility.
The responsibility rotates between the parties.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Shared means both the customer and the provider hold responsibilities in that area. Your part still requires the same attention it always did. B is wrong because no proportion is implied. The split depends on the specific service and the specific control. C is wrong because responsibilities are not optional or negotiable in that way. D is wrong because nothing rotates. Both parties hold their duties continuously.

text: A small business needs expense tracking. Several mature products already exist that meet its requirements exactly. Which service type should it choose, and why?
options: Infrastructure as a service, because it gives the most control
Software as a service, because the requirement is standard and a finished product already exists
Platform as a service, so it can customise the application
On-premises, because financial data must never leave the building
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Expense tracking is a standardised business process, and where thousands of organisations need the same thing a ready-made application almost always beats building one. A is wrong because control over an operating system is of no value here. The business wants a working expense system, not a server. C is wrong because the scenario states that existing products meet the requirements exactly, so there is nothing to build. D is wrong because the scenario states no such requirement. Inventing a compliance constraint that the question did not give you is a common way to lose marks on scenario questions.

text: Which statement best defines cloud computing?
options: The on-demand delivery of computing services such as servers, storage, databases, networking, software and analytics.
The delivery of computing services over the internet.
Storing organisational data on servers owned by another company.
Using virtual machines instead of physical servers.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. It captures both the on-demand character and the breadth of services. B is incomplete because a private cloud may deliver services over a dedicated internal network rather than the internet, so the internet is not part of the definition. C describes one use of cloud storage rather than the concept. D describes infrastructure as a service specifically, which is one service type within cloud computing.

text: An organisation runs a private cloud in its own datacentre, delivered over a dedicated internal network with no internet involvement. Is this cloud computing?
options: No, because cloud computing requires delivery over the internet.
No, because a single organisation cannot operate a cloud.
Yes, because cloud computing is defined by on-demand delivery rather than by the network used.
Yes, but only if it is connected to a public cloud.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft's definition notes that in the case of a private cloud, services are delivered through a dedicated internal network. Cloud computing is defined by how the service behaves, not by the network it travels over. A is the common misconception this question tests. B is wrong because single-organisation use is exactly what defines a private cloud. D describes hybrid cloud, which is a different arrangement.

text: Which set of responsibilities remains with the customer across on-premises, IaaS, PaaS and SaaS?
options: Operating system, applications and client devices
Physical hosts, physical network and physical datacentre
Network controls, applications and physical hosts
Customer data, configurations and settings, and identities and users
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. These are the three areas that read Customer in every column of Microsoft's published responsibility matrix. A is wrong because the operating system transfers to Microsoft at PaaS and SaaS, and client devices become Shared at SaaS. B is wrong because those three are Microsoft's responsibility in every cloud service type. C is wrong because physical hosts belong to Microsoft in all three cloud service types.

text: A company deploys a workload to Azure Virtual Machines. Who is responsible for patching the operating system?
options: Microsoft, because the workload is now in the cloud
The company, because the operating system is a customer responsibility under IaaS
Responsibility is shared equally between the two
Nobody, because Azure Virtual Machines are patched automatically
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Azure Virtual Machines is infrastructure as a service, and the operating system remains a Customer responsibility at that position. It transfers to Microsoft only at PaaS and SaaS. A is the single most common misconception about IaaS. C is wrong because the operating system is not a shared area at IaaS. D is wrong because no automatic patching is implied by creating a virtual machine.

text: Which statement about client devices in the shared responsibility model is accurate according to Microsoft's current documentation?
options: Client devices are a customer responsibility in every deployment type.
Client devices are a Microsoft responsibility in every cloud service type.
Client devices do not appear in the responsibility matrix.
Client devices are a customer responsibility for on-premises, IaaS and PaaS, and shared for SaaS.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct according to Microsoft's published matrix. This question tests a point on which much AZ-900 preparation material is imprecise: it commonly states that the customer always retains data, devices and accounts. A is the widely taught version, and it is imprecise about the matrix rather than simply wrong. Beneath the matrix Microsoft also gives a prose list of what you always retain, and endpoints appear in it, because in software as a service Microsoft may supply device management tooling while you remain responsible for endpoint protection and compliance. Shared does not mean your duty ends. For a question about the matrix, as this one is, D is the answer. B is wrong because client devices are never wholly Microsoft's. C is wrong because client devices are one of the ten listed responsibility areas.

text: A private cloud is hosted in a dedicated datacentre operated by a third party on behalf of one organisation. Which statement is correct?
options: It is a private cloud, because a single organisation uses it.
It is not a private cloud, because it is not on the organisation's own site.
It is a public cloud, because a third party operates it.
It is a hybrid cloud, because two parties are involved.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Being used by a single organisation is what makes a cloud private, not its physical location. B is the common misconception. C is wrong because general availability to any purchaser defines a public cloud. D is wrong because hybrid means combining public and private environments.

text: An organisation runs its main applications on Azure and a specialised workload on a second public cloud provider. What is this arrangement called?
options: Hybrid cloud
Multicloud
Private cloud
Azure Arc
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Multicloud means using two or more public cloud providers. A is wrong because hybrid combines public and private, and no private environment is described. C is wrong because neither environment is dedicated to one organisation. D is wrong because Azure Arc is a management technology, not a cloud model.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, which resource types hosted outside Azure can Azure Arc manage?
options: Only Windows servers
Any resource type that exists in Azure
Servers and virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services, and SQL Server
Only Kubernetes clusters
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft’s current overview names four resource types hosted outside Azure: servers and virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services, and SQL Server. Note that Arc-enabled data services such as SQL Managed Instance run on an Arc-enabled Kubernetes cluster, whereas Arc-enabled SQL Server needs no Kubernetes and is projected directly from an agent on the host machine. A is wrong because Linux servers are explicitly included. B is wrong because the list is specific rather than unlimited. Arc names four resource types; it does not extend to every Azure resource type. D is wrong because it omits servers and virtual machines, the most commonly used of the four, as well as the two database entries.

text: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure?
options: Signing up for a cloud service
Leasing a company vehicle
Building a datacentre
Renting a convention centre
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Capital expenditure is a one-time, up-front expenditure to purchase or secure tangible resources. A is operational expenditure, paid over time. B is wrong because leasing is payment for use over time, not a purchase producing an owned asset. D is wrong for the same reason. Renting a venue is spending on a service over time.

text: Why is cloud computing classified as operational expenditure?
options: Because it operates on a consumption-based model, paying for resources used over time
Because it is always cheaper than owning hardware
Because cloud resources are intangible
Because cloud providers do not accept up-front payment
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Cloud computing is operational expenditure precisely because it operates on a consumption-based model. B is wrong because cloud computing is not automatically cheaper; a poorly managed estate can cost more than owned hardware. C is wrong because tangibility is not the test. D is wrong because up-front payment options do exist, for example when purchasing a reservation.

text: An organisation running its own datacentre underestimates its future capacity needs. What is the consequence?
options: It wastes money on capacity that sits idle.
Its costs automatically adjust downwards.
There is no consequence, because capacity can be added instantly.
The datacentre reaches capacity and applications may suffer decreased performance.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Underestimating means the datacentre quickly reaches capacity, and fixing it requires ordering, receiving and installing hardware, plus adding power, cooling and networking. A describes the consequence of overestimating. B is a property of the consumption-based model, not of owned hardware. C is wrong because adding physical capacity takes weeks or months.

text: A student stops a virtual machine at the end of a lab exercise but does not delete it. What is the billing outcome?
options: All charges associated with the virtual machine stop.
Compute charges stop, but the attached disk continues to be billed as storage.
Charges continue exactly as before.
Charges stop only at the end of the billing month.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Stopping a virtual machine stops the compute charge, but the disk holding the operating system continues to exist and continues to be billed. A is the assumption that produces unexpected bills. Stopping is not the same as deleting. C is wrong because the compute charge, usually the largest component, does stop. D is wrong because billing is by consumption, not by calendar month.

text: An organisation has a steady overall level of compute spend, but the specific virtual machine sizes and regions it uses change from quarter to quarter. Which pricing arrangement fits best?
options: Azure reservations
Spot pricing
Azure savings plan for compute
Pay-as-you-go
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A savings plan commits to an hourly amount of compute spend rather than to a specific resource, and the benefit applies automatically across eligible compute usage. A is wrong because a reservation is tied to a specific resource configuration. B is wrong because spot workloads can be evicted at any time, which is unrelated to the steadiness described. D is wrong because the organisation would pay the highest rate despite having predictable spend.

text: Which workload is most appropriate for Azure spot pricing?
options: A public-facing e-commerce website
A database serving live customer transactions
A company's primary email system
An overnight batch job that can be restarted if interrupted
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Spot pricing offers deep discounts on spare capacity in exchange for accepting that the workload can be evicted with short warning, so it suits interruptible work. A, B and C are all wrong for the same reason: each is a service users depend on continuously, and being switched off without warning would cause a direct problem. The correct mental test is simple: if being switched off without warning would cause a problem, spot is the wrong choice. Note that spot is not merely a cheaper rate. It is a cheaper rate with a condition attached.

text: Which statement about serverless computing is correct?
options: No servers are involved in running the code.
Servers are involved, but the customer does not provision, patch or manage them.
The customer must specify how many instances to run.
Serverless is always cheaper than a virtual machine.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The code runs on physical hardware in a Microsoft datacentre. What the term describes is the absence of servers from the customer's responsibilities. A is the misconception the name creates. C is wrong because automatic scaling is a defining characteristic of serverless. D is wrong because at steady, continuous, high utilisation a reserved virtual machine is usually cheaper, since serverless saves money by charging nothing when idle.

text: An organisation wants its web application to remain reachable even if one datacentre in a region suffers a power failure. Which benefit is being described?
options: Scalability
Elasticity
Agility
High availability
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. The stated goal is to keep the application reachable through a failure, which is the defining purpose of high availability. A is wrong because scalability concerns having enough capacity for the load, and no change in demand is described. B is wrong because elasticity is automatic scaling in response to demand. C is wrong because agility concerns the speed of deploying and changing resources.

text: A retailer adds more identical web servers behind a load balancer to handle a traffic surge. Which type of scaling is this?
options: Vertical scaling
Horizontal scaling
Scaling up
Elasticity
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Adding more instances is horizontal scaling, also called scaling out. A and C are the same answer expressed two ways, and both are wrong because vertical scaling changes the size of a single instance rather than the number of instances. D is wrong because the scenario describes a deliberate action rather than automatic adjustment by the platform. The signal in a question is usually the verb: adding servers points to scaling out.

text: A service level agreement commits to 99.9 percent uptime. Approximately how much downtime does that permit in a 30-day month?
options: About 4 minutes
About 22 minutes
About 43 minutes
About 7 hours
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Subtracting 99.9 from 100 leaves 0.1 percent. One tenth of one percent of 43,200 minutes is about 43 minutes. A corresponds to 99.99 percent. B corresponds to 99.95 percent. D corresponds to 99 percent. The lesson is that percentages which look nearly identical permit very different amounts of downtime.

text: Which statement best describes reliability as a benefit of cloud computing?
options: The ability to adjust capacity automatically in response to demand
The ability of a system to recover from failure and continue to function
The ability to predict and forecast what a cloud environment will cost
The ability to deploy and change resources quickly as requirements change
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Reliability is the ability of a system to recover from failures and continue to function, supported principally through global scale. A describes elasticity. C describes cost predictability, which is one half of predictability. D describes agility. All three distractors are genuine cloud benefits, which is what makes this a test of precision rather than recall.

text: An administrator uses PowerShell to create resources in Azure. Which aspect of manageability is this?
options: Management in the cloud
Management of the cloud
Governance
Predictability
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Management in the cloud describes how you interact with the environment: through a portal, a command line interface, application programming interfaces, or PowerShell. B is wrong because management of the cloud describes what is managed, such as automatic scaling, template deployment, health monitoring and alerts. The distinction is of against in. C is wrong because governance concerns compliance with rules rather than the method of interaction. D is wrong because predictability concerns confidence about performance and cost.

text: An organisation wants non-compliant resources to be identified automatically and corrected without an administrator intervening. Which cloud benefit does this describe?
options: Security
Manageability
Governance
High availability
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Governance concerns whether an environment follows the rules. Cloud auditing can flag resources out of compliance and apply mitigation automatically. A is wrong because security concerns protecting the environment rather than checking it against rules, although the two support each other. B is wrong because manageability concerns how an environment is administered. D is wrong because high availability concerns staying operational through failure.

text: A website remains online during a zone failure but responds very slowly because it has too few instances for the traffic. Which statement is accurate?
options: The site is highly available but under-scaled.
The site is scalable but not highly available.
The site is neither highly available nor scalable.
The site is elastic.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Surviving a zone failure is high availability. Responding slowly for want of instances is a shortfall in scalability. The two properties are independent. B reverses them. C is wrong because the site demonstrably survived the failure. D is wrong because an elastic system would have added capacity automatically as demand rose.

text: Which service type gives the customer the greatest control over the environment?
options: Software as a service
Platform as a service
Infrastructure as a service
All three give equal control
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Infrastructure as a service provides servers, storage and networks, with the customer managing operating systems, applications and data. A is wrong because software as a service gives the least control. B is a middle position; the operating system has already moved to the provider. D is wrong because the three types are three positions on a scale of control.

text: Which of the following is a Microsoft-published example of platform as a service in Azure?
options: Azure Virtual Machines
Azure App Service
Azure Disk Storage
Microsoft 365
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Microsoft names Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Azure SQL Database and Azure Storage as its platform as a service examples. A is named as an infrastructure as a service example. C is also named as an infrastructure as a service example. D is named as a software as a service example.

text: A company must move a fifteen-year-old application to the cloud. It requires a specific operating system version and particular installed software, and cannot be rewritten. Which service type should be used?
options: Infrastructure as a service
Platform as a service
Software as a service
The application cannot move to the cloud
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. The scenario states a requirement for specific operating system configuration, and only infrastructure as a service gives control of the operating system. This is also the classic lift and shift case. B is wrong because platform as a service removes operating system control. C is wrong because the organisation has its own application to run. D is wrong because infrastructure as a service exists for exactly this situation.

text: An academy uses Microsoft 365 for staff email and documents. What does the academy remain responsible for?
options: Nothing, because the provider operates the application
The operating system underneath the service
Patching the application
Its data, its configuration and its user identities
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Microsoft 365 is software as a service, and customer data, configurations and settings, and identities and users remain Customer responsibilities at every position on the scale. A is the most dangerous misconception in this block, and it is why account compromise remains a customer-side risk in software as a service. B is a Microsoft responsibility at software as a service. C is also a Microsoft responsibility at software as a service.

text: According to Microsoft's published documentation, which service type does Azure Storage belong to?
options: Infrastructure as a service
Platform as a service
Software as a service
It is not classified
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Microsoft lists Azure Storage among its platform as a service examples. A is what a substantial amount of third-party material claims, reasoning that storage sounds like infrastructure. Note that Azure Disk Storage is a separate service and is listed under infrastructure as a service. C is wrong because Azure Storage is not a finished application a user signs in to. D is wrong because the underlying principle is that classification depends on how much of the stack you manage, not on what the service is made of.

text: Which statement about the relationship between control and management responsibility is correct?
options: As control increases, management responsibility decreases.
Control and management responsibility are unrelated.
As control increases, management responsibility also increases.
Platform as a service offers the most control and the least management effort.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. The two move together. Infrastructure as a service offers the most control and requires the most management; software as a service offers the least of both. A reverses the relationship, describing an arrangement that does not exist. B is wrong because the relationship is the central idea of the service types. D is wrong because no position offers both extremes, and an option claiming otherwise is testing whether you know that.

text: An organisation runs its website on Azure App Service, stores data in Azure SQL Database, runs a legacy tool on an Azure virtual machine, and uses Microsoft 365 for staff email. Which statement is accurate?
options: The organisation has made an architectural error by mixing service types.
The organisation should standardise on infrastructure as a service.
The organisation is using a combination of service models, which is normal.
The organisation is using platform as a service only.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft states that many Azure solutions use a combination of service models. Choosing the right position on the scale for each workload is what competent architecture looks like. A is wrong because mixing is normal and usually correct. B is wrong because it would move the website and database backwards into a position requiring operating system management for no benefit. D is wrong because a virtual machine is IaaS and Microsoft 365 is SaaS.

text: Under platform as a service, applications and network controls are listed as shared responsibilities. What does shared mean?
options: The responsibility is divided exactly in half.
Both parties hold duties in that area, and the customer's duties still require attention.
Either party may choose to take the responsibility.
The responsibility rotates between the parties.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Shared means both the customer and the provider hold responsibilities in that area. Your part still requires the same attention it always did. A is wrong because no proportion is implied; the split depends on the specific service and control. C is wrong because responsibilities are not optional or negotiable. D is wrong because nothing rotates. Both parties hold their duties continuously.

text: Which statement about resource groups is correct?
options: A resource group can contain other resource groups.
All resources in a resource group must be in the same region.
A resource cannot be moved between resource groups.
A resource must belong to exactly one resource group.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct because every resource in Azure belongs to exactly one resource group, and cannot exist outside one or belong to two. A is wrong because resource groups cannot be nested. This is the most commonly confused rule in the topic. Management groups can be nested; resource groups cannot. B is wrong because a single resource group can hold resources located in different regions. The group's own region only stores its metadata. C is wrong because most resources can be moved to a different resource group, although not every resource type supports it.

text: An organisation needs to apply one policy to forty subscriptions at the same time. Which Azure construct should it use?
options: A resource group
A region pair
An availability zone
A management group
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct because a management group contains subscriptions, and settings applied at the management group are inherited by every subscription inside it. This is precisely the problem management groups exist to solve. A is wrong because a resource group sits below the subscription, not above it. It cannot apply anything to a subscription. B is wrong because a region pair concerns recovery sequencing and update staggering, not policy application. C is wrong because an availability zone is a physical grouping of datacentres within a region and has no role in governance.

text: What is the minimum number of availability zones provided in an Azure region that supports them?
options: One
Two
Three
Six
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft provides a minimum of three separate availability zones in every region that supports them, so that a service can lose one zone and still have two remaining. A is wrong because a single zone would provide no protection against the loss of a datacentre. B is wrong because two is not the stated minimum, even though two would technically allow one failure. D is wrong because six is the maximum nesting depth for management groups, not a zone count. This distractor tests whether you have confused two unrelated numbers.

text: A virtual machine must be placed in a specific availability zone chosen by the administrator. What category of service is this?
options: A zone-redundant service
A zonal service
An always-available service
A sovereign service
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A zonal service is pinned to one zone that you select, and a virtual machine is the standard example. Resilience is your responsibility, achieved by creating several virtual machines across different zones. A is wrong because a zone-redundant service is replicated or distributed across zones by the service itself. Zone-redundant storage is the standard example. C is wrong because an always-available service runs across all regions and is not tied to zones at all. Microsoft Entra ID is the standard example. D is not a real category. Sovereign describes isolated cloud instances such as Azure Government, not a way of using zones.

text: Which pair of statements correctly describes the two purposes of an Azure subscription?
options: A billing boundary and an access boundary
A physical location and a legal boundary
A container for management groups and a policy boundary
A network boundary and a storage boundary
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. A subscription aggregates usage for invoicing, and permissions applied at subscription level are inherited by everything inside it. B is wrong because a subscription is a logical container, not a physical location. Regions and datacentres describe physical location. C is wrong because the containment runs the other way. A management group contains subscriptions, not the reverse. D is wrong because networking and storage are services created inside a subscription, not the purposes the subscription serves.

text: Which statement about Azure region pairing is correct?
options: Every Azure region is paired with another region.
Many Azure regions are not paired, and use availability zones as their primary means of redundancy.
Microsoft applies planned updates to both regions in a pair simultaneously.
Paired regions are always in different geographies for maximum separation.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Microsoft's documentation states that many regions are nonpaired and rely on availability zones instead. Poland Central, Qatar Central and Italy North are examples of nonpaired regions. A is wrong, and this is the single most common outdated belief about this topic. Older training material often presents pairing as universal. It is not. C is wrong because it states the opposite of the actual behaviour. Updates are staggered across a pair, one region at a time, precisely so that a faulty update cannot affect both. D is wrong because almost all paired regions sit within the same geography, which supports data residency. Brazil South, paired with South Central US, is the best-known exception.

text: What is the maximum depth to which management groups can be nested, excluding the root management group and the subscription level?
options: Three levels
Ten levels
There is no limit
Six levels
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Management groups support six levels of nesting, not counting the root management group and not counting the subscription level. A is wrong as a hard limit, although it is a reasonable design target. Microsoft recommends keeping hierarchies to about three or four levels in practice, but the permitted maximum is six. B is wrong because ten thousand is the number of management groups permitted in a directory, which is a different limit entirely. C is wrong because a definite limit exists.

text: A policy is applied to a management group that contains three subscriptions. Which resources are affected?
options: Only resources created after the policy was applied
Only the three subscriptions themselves, not their contents
Every resource group and every resource within all three subscriptions
Only resources in the first subscription in the group
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Settings inherit downwards through every level of the hierarchy, reaching subscriptions, then resource groups, then individual resources. A is wrong because inheritance applies to the existing contents of the hierarchy, not only to newly created items. B is wrong because it stops the inheritance one level too early. The whole purpose of the structure is that settings flow all the way down. D is wrong because inheritance applies to every child of the management group, not to one arbitrary subscription.

text: Which statement correctly describes a sovereign region such as Azure Government?
options: It is a physically and logically isolated instance of Azure with its own compliance boundary.
It is a normal Azure region with additional security settings applied.
It is an availability zone reserved for government workloads.
It is a region pair operated by a national government.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Sovereign clouds are separate instances of Azure, with their own portals and service catalogues, and in the case of Azure operated by 21Vianet, a separate operating company. B is wrong because the isolation is structural, not a matter of configuration. You cannot turn a normal region into a sovereign one by changing settings. C is wrong because availability zones are about physical resilience within a region and have nothing to do with sovereignty. D is wrong because a region pair is a relationship between two regions, and sovereign clouds are operated by Microsoft or its licensed partner, not by a government.

text: A resource group named rg-lab is created in South Africa North. A virtual machine inside it is created in West Europe. What is the outcome?
options: The creation fails, because resources must match the group's region.
The virtual machine is automatically relocated to South Africa North.
The creation succeeds. The group's region stores its metadata only.
The creation succeeds, but the resource group changes region to West Europe.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A resource group's region determines where information about the group is stored. It does not restrict where the resources inside it may run. A is wrong because no such restriction exists. This is one of the most commonly held misconceptions about resource groups. B is wrong because Azure never silently moves a resource to a different region. Region is chosen by you at creation. D is wrong because a resource group's region is set when it is created and cannot be changed afterwards. Professional refinement beyond the exam answer: although the deployment succeeds, control plane operations for the group are routed through South Africa North. If that region had an outage, the virtual machine would keep running in West Europe but you would be unable to modify or delete it until the metadata region recovered.

text: Which Azure constructs can be nested inside another instance of themselves? Choose the correct statement.
options: Management groups can be nested; resource groups cannot.
Both management groups and resource groups can be nested.
Resource groups can be nested; management groups cannot.
Neither can be nested.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Management groups nest up to six levels deep. Resource groups cannot contain other resource groups. B is wrong because it credits resource groups with a capability they do not have. C is wrong because it reverses the two, which is the single most common error in this topic. D is wrong because management groups genuinely do nest, and that nesting is the reason they are useful for large organisations.

text: An organisation wants each of its three departments to receive a separate invoice for its Azure usage. What should it use?
options: Three resource groups
Three subscriptions
Three availability zones
Three regions
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The subscription is the billing boundary, so usage is aggregated and invoiced per subscription. Separate subscriptions produce separate invoices. A is wrong because resource groups organise resources for management purposes but are not the unit of invoicing. C is wrong because availability zones concern physical resilience and have no billing function. D is wrong because although costs vary between regions, the region is not the unit on which invoices are issued.

text: A team deploys its application into a region that has a paired region. What does this pairing guarantee?
options: Automatic failover to the paired region if the primary region fails.
Automatic high availability with no further configuration.
Recovery sequencing and staggered updates, but resilience must still be designed.
That all data is automatically replicated to the paired region.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Pairing provides recovery sequencing, staggered platform updates and data residency alignment. Microsoft states explicitly that deploying into a paired region does not by itself make resources more resilient. A is wrong because failover is not automatic. Even where a service supports Microsoft-managed failover, it is performed only in catastrophic situations after repeated failed recovery attempts. B is wrong for the same reason. High availability is something you design and configure, not something pairing provides. D is wrong because only a small number of services, such as geo-redundant storage, replicate to the paired region, and that behaviour must be configured through the service.

text: What is the essential difference between a container and a virtual machine?
options: Each virtual machine carries its own operating system, while containers share the host operating system.
A container runs faster because it uses more processor cores.
Containers cannot run Linux applications.
A virtual machine can be scaled automatically and a container cannot.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. The duplication of the operating system is the essential difference, and everything else follows from it: containers are smaller, start faster, and fit more workloads onto the same hardware. B is wrong because containers do not receive more processor resources. Their speed advantage comes from not booting an operating system. C is wrong because containers run Linux applications very commonly. D is wrong because both can be scaled. Scale sets scale virtual machines and container platforms scale containers.

text: An organisation needs to run a piece of code whenever a file is uploaded to storage. The code runs for a few seconds and nothing happens between uploads. Which compute type suits this?
options: A virtual machine
A container
A function
An availability set
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A function runs in response to an event, scales with the number of events, and charges only for execution. Nothing runs between uploads, so nothing is charged. A is wrong because a virtual machine would sit idle between uploads and bill continuously for capacity doing nothing. B is wrong because although a container could do this, it is heavier than needed for a few seconds of event-driven work. D is wrong because an availability set is a high availability arrangement for virtual machines, not a compute type.

text: How many fault domains and update domains can an availability set have?
options: Up to 3 fault domains and up to 20 update domains
Up to 20 fault domains and up to 3 update domains
Up to 5 fault domains and up to 5 update domains
Unlimited fault domains and up to 10 update domains
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Each availability set can have up to 3 fault domains and 20 update domains, and these settings cannot be changed after creation. B is wrong because it reverses the two numbers, which is the most common error on this point. C is wrong, although five is the number Microsoft uses in its worked example of update domain wrap-around, which is where the confusion comes from. D is wrong because both values have definite limits.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, what is recommended for high availability of virtual machines?
options: Availability sets, because they are the traditional approach
A single large virtual machine, because fewer components fail
Virtual Machine Scale Sets with Flexible orchestration mode
Azure Virtual Desktop
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft recommends scale sets with Flexible orchestration for high availability, describing it as offering the widest range of features. A is what a great deal of AZ-900 material still says, and it reflects guidance that has been superseded. Availability sets still work and remain examinable, but they are no longer the recommendation. B is wrong because a single virtual machine of any size provides no protection against failure at all. D is wrong because Azure Virtual Desktop is a desktop virtualisation service, not a high availability mechanism.

text: Which mechanism provides the highest reliability for virtual machines?
options: Availability sets
Update domains
Fault domains
Availability zones
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Microsoft states that availability zones have the highest reliability, because each virtual machine is deployed in a physically separate datacentre with independent power, networking and cooling. A is wrong because availability sets provide high availability but do not offer the same level of resiliency as availability zones. They remain susceptible to datacentre-level failures. B is wrong because update domains are a component of an availability set rather than a mechanism in their own right. C is wrong for the same reason. Fault domains are a component of an availability set.

text: What is the minimum number of network interfaces a virtual machine must have?
options: One
Zero, because a network interface is optional
Two, one for private and one for public traffic
It depends on the operating system
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. A virtual machine must have at least one network interface, and may have more depending on its size. B is wrong because the network interface is the interconnection between the machine and the virtual network, so it is required. C is wrong because a public IP address is an optional resource that attaches to an existing interface, not a reason for a second one. D is wrong because the requirement is the same regardless of operating system. The number of interfaces supported depends on the virtual machine size.

text: Which of the following is an optional rather than required resource for a virtual machine?
options: A network interface
A virtual network
An operating system disk
A public IP address
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. A public IP address is needed only if the machine must be reachable directly from the internet, and many virtual machines should not have one. A is wrong because at least one network interface is required. B is wrong because a virtual network is required. It provides the private address space the machine sits in. C is wrong because the operating system disk holds the operating system and boot files, without which the machine cannot start.

text: A scale set is created in Uniform orchestration mode. The team later decides Flexible would have been better. What must be done?
options: Change the orchestration mode in the scale set settings.
Stop the scale set, change the mode, then restart it.
Recreate the scale set, because the orchestration mode cannot be changed after creation.
Add a second orchestration mode alongside the first.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft states explicitly that the orchestration mode is defined when the scale set is created and cannot be changed or updated later. A is wrong because no such setting can be altered afterwards. B is wrong because stopping the scale set does not make the mode changeable. D is wrong because a scale set has exactly one orchestration mode.

text: Which statement about Azure Virtual Desktop multi-session is correct?
options: It allows one user to open several desktops at once.
It allows several users to share one virtual machine at the same time, and is exclusive to Azure Virtual Desktop.
It is available on any Windows client installation.
It requires a separate virtual machine for each user.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Multi-session allows several users on one virtual machine simultaneously, and Microsoft describes the Windows 11 and Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session capability as exclusive to Azure Virtual Desktop. It is where the cost saving comes from, because it reduces the number of virtual machines needed. A is wrong because multi-session concerns multiple users, not multiple desktops for one user. C is wrong because the capability is exclusive to this service. D is wrong because that describes single-session, which is the other option.

text: A team is building a web application and has no requirement for operating system control. Which hosting option does Microsoft describe as ideal?
options: Azure Virtual Machines
Azure Container Instances
Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure App Service
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure App Service provides fully managed hosting for web applications and is optimised for them. Microsoft's guidance is that when building web applications, App Service is an ideal option. A is wrong because a virtual machine would require the team to manage an operating system they have said they do not need to control. B is wrong because Container Instances is a lower-level building block without scaling or load balancing. C is wrong because Kubernetes Service suits teams requiring full control of Kubernetes, which is far beyond what is described.

text: A team wants to run containerised microservices that scale with demand, including scaling to zero, without managing a Kubernetes cluster. Which service fits?
options: Azure Container Instances
Azure Container Apps
Azure Kubernetes Service
Azure Virtual Machines
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct.
