A is wrong because deny prevents the request outright, which is exactly what the scenario says it does not want yet. C is wrong because modify alters requests, for example by adding a tag, rather than reporting on non-compliance. D is wrong because a disabled policy is not evaluated at all, so it would report nothing.

text: What is an Azure Policy initiative?
options: A group of policy definitions treated as one assignable unit.
The act of attaching a policy to a scope.
A single business rule expressed in JSON.
A report showing which resources are non-compliant.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. An initiative, also called a policy set, groups several definitions so they can be managed and assigned together. Regulatory standards are commonly published as initiatives, because compliance with a standard requires many individual rules. C describes a policy definition, which is the individual rule an initiative contains. B describes an assignment, which is the third term in this structure. D describes the compliance dashboard or a compliance report rather than an initiative.

text: At which scopes can an Azure Policy definition or initiative be assigned?
options: Subscriptions only
Resource groups and resources only
Management groups, subscriptions, resource groups or individual resources
Management groups only
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A definition or initiative can be assigned to any scope Azure supports, and the assignment applies to all resources within that scope, with subscopes excluded where necessary. This is the hierarchy from Module 5, now carrying governance rules. A, B and D are each wrong because they exclude scopes that are in fact supported. The full hierarchy is available, which is what makes it possible to apply one rule to an entire organisation.

text: An organisation needs learner records protected so that no administrator can accidentally delete the storage account, while the records team can still manage its configuration. Which mechanism achieves this?
options: An Azure Policy with a deny effect
A ReadOnly lock
Removing everyone's Owner role
A CanNotDelete lock
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. CanNotDelete permits reading and modification while preventing deletion, and it overrides user permissions so that even an Owner cannot delete the account. A is wrong because Azure Policy governs how resources are configured rather than whether an existing resource may be deleted. B is wrong because ReadOnly would also block the configuration management the scenario requires. It is more restrictive than the requirement. C is wrong because it would not protect against a mistake made by whoever retains the necessary permissions, and somebody must retain them.

text: Which statement about Azure Blueprints is currently accurate?
options: It is the recommended service for deploying governed environments in Azure.
It is being retired, and Microsoft recommends Deployment Stacks with template specs instead.
It has been renamed Azure Policy.
It is a feature of Microsoft Purview.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Azure Blueprints never left preview and is being retired, with full retirement on 31 January 2027 and a phased withdrawal that began on 31 July 2026. Microsoft recommends Azure Deployment Stacks together with template specs or templates in source control. A is what a great deal of third-party AZ-900 material still says, and should be treated as dated. C is wrong because Azure Policy is a separate service that continues to exist. Blueprints could include policy assignments, but the two are not the same thing. D is wrong because Blueprints concerned Azure resource deployment, not the data estate.

text: Which statement best describes the relationship between Azure Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell?
options: Cloud Shell is a browser-based terminal in which either Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell can be used.
They are three alternative tools that do different jobs.
Cloud Shell replaced Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell.
Azure CLI runs on Linux and Azure PowerShell runs on Windows, and Cloud Shell runs on neither.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Cloud Shell is a place: an interactive, authenticated, browser-accessible terminal offering a choice of Bash or PowerShell. The command line interface and Azure PowerShell are the command sets you use within it. B is wrong because the command line interface and PowerShell do the same job in different syntax, and Cloud Shell is where either can be run. C is wrong because both remain current and can also be installed locally. D is wrong because both tools are cross-platform, running on Windows, Linux and macOS, and Cloud Shell runs on Azure Linux.

text: After how long without interactive activity does a Cloud Shell session time out?
options: 5 minutes
20 minutes
60 minutes
It does not time out
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A Cloud Shell session times out after 20 minutes without interactive activity. A is wrong, although 5 GB is the size of the file share used when storage is attached, which is where the number 5 comes from in this topic. C is wrong because the timeout is considerably shorter than an hour. D is wrong because Cloud Shell runs on a temporary host provided per session, so it does time out.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, does Azure Cloud Shell require a storage account?
options: Yes, always. Cloud Shell cannot start without one.
Yes, but only when using PowerShell mode.
No. An ephemeral session can be started without storage, but files do not persist.
No, and files persist regardless.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft's current documentation states that when starting Cloud Shell you have the option of using it with or without an attached storage account. Continuing without storage is called an ephemeral session, and files saved during it are deleted when the window closes. A is what almost every AZ-900 guide still says, and it reflects the older arrangement. If an exam question assumes it, answer as the question expects, but know the current position. B is wrong because the choice does not depend on which shell is selected. D is wrong because persistence is exactly what an ephemeral session does not provide. Attaching storage is what persists files, using a 5 GB file share.

text: An organisation wants to manage Windows and Linux servers running in its own datacentre using Azure tools, without moving them to Azure. Which service enables this?
options: Azure Resource Manager
Azure Migrate
Azure Cloud Shell
Azure Arc
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure Arc projects existing non-Azure and on-premises resources into Azure Resource Manager, so they can be managed with Azure tools while continuing to run where they are. A is wrong because Resource Manager is the management service that Arc projects resources into. It does not by itself reach outside Azure. B is wrong because Azure Migrate, covered in Module 8, discovers, assesses and migrates workloads. Migration is precisely what this organisation does not want. C is wrong because Cloud Shell is a terminal for running commands, not a mechanism for extending management to other environments.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, which resource types hosted outside Azure can Azure Arc manage?
options: Servers and virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters, Azure data services, and SQL Server
Only Windows servers
Only Kubernetes clusters
Any resource type that exists in Azure
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Microsoft’s current documentation names four resource types hosted outside Azure: servers and virtual machines, meaning Windows and Linux physical servers and virtual machines; Kubernetes clusters running anywhere across multiple supported distributions; Azure data services; and SQL Server. B is wrong because Linux servers are explicitly included. C is wrong because it omits servers and virtual machines, which are the most commonly used of the four, as well as the two database entries. D is wrong because the list is specific rather than unlimited. Arc names four resource types; it does not extend to every Azure resource type.

text: What does Azure Arc do with the resources it manages?
options: It migrates them into an Azure datacentre.
It creates copies of them in Azure.
It projects them into Azure Resource Manager, so they appear as Azure resources while continuing to run where they are.
It converts them into Azure virtual machines.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Arc projects existing non-Azure and on-premises resources into Azure Resource Manager. Each connected resource appears as its own resource there and can be organised with resource groups and tags. Nothing moves. A is wrong, and it is the most common misconception about Arc. It moves management, not workloads. B is wrong because no copy is made. The resource itself becomes visible and manageable. D is wrong because no conversion takes place. A server in a datacentre remains a server in a datacentre.

text: Which of the following best describes infrastructure as code?
options: Defining infrastructure in files that can be version-controlled, reviewed and deployed repeatedly.
Using a graphical interface to configure infrastructure more quickly.
Writing application code that runs on cloud infrastructure.
Installing code libraries onto virtual machines automatically.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Infrastructure as code means defining the infrastructure in code, storing that code in a source repository and versioning it, so that anyone on the team can deploy a consistent environment from it. C is wrong because it describes ordinary application development. Infrastructure as code concerns the infrastructure itself, not what runs on it. B is wrong because a graphical interface is the alternative to infrastructure as code, not a form of it. D is wrong because installing software onto machines is configuration management rather than defining the infrastructure.

text: What is the difference between a declarative and an imperative approach to deployment?
options: Declarative states the steps to perform; imperative states the desired end state.
Declarative states the desired end state; imperative states the steps to perform.
Declarative applies to Azure; imperative applies to other clouds.
There is no practical difference.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A declarative definition describes what you want and leaves the system to determine the steps. An imperative script describes how to get there, step by step. ARM templates and Bicep are declarative; command line and PowerShell scripts are imperative. A is wrong because it reverses the two, which is the most common error on this point. C is wrong because both approaches exist on every platform. The distinction is about how a deployment is expressed. D is wrong because the difference is practical and significant, most visibly in what happens when a deployment is run a second time.

text: An ARM template is deployed. The same template is then deployed again without any changes. What happens?
options: The deployment fails, because the resources already exist.
Duplicate resources are created.
The existing resources are deleted and recreated.
The deployment succeeds and the resources remain in the same state, because templates are idempotent.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Microsoft states that templates are idempotent, meaning you can deploy the same template many times and get the same resource types in the same state. This is the practical advantage of a declarative approach. A is wrong, and it describes what a naive imperative script would typically do. B is wrong because the template names the resources, so redeploying refers to the same ones rather than creating new ones. C is wrong because Resource Manager does not destroy and recreate resources that already match the desired state.

text: What is Azure Resource Manager?
options: A tool for writing ARM templates.
The deployment and management service through which every request to create, update or delete an Azure resource passes.
A monitoring service for Azure resources.
The graphical interface used to manage Azure.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Azure Resource Manager is the deployment and management service for Azure. The portal, the command line interface, PowerShell, the interfaces and templates are all clients of it, which is why they produce identical results. A is wrong because templates are written in an editor. Resource Manager is the service that receives and acts on them. C is wrong because monitoring is provided by Azure Monitor, covered in Module 13. D describes the Azure portal, which is one of several clients of Resource Manager rather than Resource Manager itself.

text: In what format is an ARM template written?
options: YAML
XML
JSON
PowerShell script
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. An ARM template is a JavaScript Object Notation file, usually shortened to JSON, that defines the infrastructure and configuration for a project using declarative syntax. A is wrong, although YAML is used by other infrastructure as code tools and by Azure pipeline definitions. B is wrong because XML is not used for ARM templates. D is wrong because a PowerShell script is imperative, describing steps rather than declaring an end state.

text: What is the relationship between Bicep and ARM templates?
options: Bicep replaced ARM templates, which are no longer supported.
Bicep is a different service that competes with Azure Resource Manager.
Bicep is a language with simpler syntax; each Bicep file is automatically converted to an ARM template during deployment.
Bicep is an imperative alternative to declarative ARM templates.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Bicep is a domain-specific language offering the same capabilities as ARM templates with easier syntax, and each Bicep file is automatically converted to an ARM template during deployment. Microsoft recommends looking at Bicep if you are considering infrastructure as code options. A is wrong because ARM templates remain fully supported, and Bicep produces one at deployment time. B is wrong because Bicep deploys through Azure Resource Manager like everything else. It does not compete with it. D is wrong because Bicep is declarative, using declarative syntax exactly as ARM templates do.

text: An administrator needs to create fifty identical test environments, each of which must match exactly. Which approach is most appropriate?
options: Creating each one in the Azure portal, following a written checklist.
Using Azure Arc to project the environments into Azure.
Writing a Cloud Shell command for each resource and running them by hand.
Deploying an ARM template or Bicep file fifty times.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. A declarative definition produces the same environment every time, which is exactly what identical environments require. Templates are idempotent and repeatable, and the definition doubles as the record of what was deployed. A is wrong because a hand-built environment depends on the person following the checklist perfectly fifty times. Any deviation is invisible until something behaves differently. B is wrong because Arc projects existing resources hosted outside Azure into Azure management. It does not create environments. C is wrong because running commands by hand is imperative and error-prone at that repetition, although scripting them would be better than the portal.

text: Which service analyses your resource configuration and usage, then recommends improvements?
options: Azure Advisor
Azure Service Health
Azure Monitor
Microsoft Purview
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Azure Advisor analyses resource configuration and usage telemetry and recommends solutions, which is why Microsoft describes it as a personalised cloud consultant. B is wrong because Service Health reports issues with Azure itself rather than with your configuration. C is wrong because Azure Monitor collects and analyses telemetry about what your resources are doing. It reports facts rather than making recommendations. D is wrong because Microsoft Purview governs the data estate, as covered in Module 11.

text: Which of the following is one of Azure Advisor's five recommendation categories?
options: Compliance
Operational excellence
Governance
Availability zones
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The five categories are reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence. A is wrong because compliance is not an Advisor category, although Microsoft Purview and Azure Policy both concern compliance. C is wrong because governance is the subject of Module 11 rather than an Advisor category. D is wrong because availability zones are a resilience mechanism from Module 5, not a recommendation category.

text: A widespread Azure outage is affecting many customers globally. Which component reports this publicly, without requiring sign-in?
options: Resource Health
Service Health
Azure Status
Azure Monitor
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Azure Status is a public page reporting Azure issues with widespread impact, visible to anyone without signing in. A is wrong because Resource Health reports the health of your individual resources and requires access to them. B is wrong because Service Health is personalised to your subscriptions and requires sign-in. It is the right answer for issues affecting the services you use, but not for a public global view. D is wrong because Azure Monitor reports on your own resources rather than on Azure's own service status.

text: An organisation wants to be told only about Azure issues affecting the specific services and regions its subscriptions use. Which component provides this?
options: Azure Status
Azure Advisor
Application Insights
Service Health
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Service Health reports issues affecting the specific services and regions your subscriptions actually use, and is personalised rather than global. A is wrong because Azure Status is a global public view. It would report issues irrelevant to this organisation and might omit ones that matter to it. B is wrong because Advisor recommends improvements to your own configuration. C is wrong because Application Insights monitors application performance rather than Azure's service status.

text: Microsoft is retiring a service the organisation depends on. Where would this be communicated, and how far in advance?
options: As a service issue, communicated when the retirement occurs
As a health advisory, communicated at least 90 days in advance
As an Advisor recommendation, communicated immediately
Retirements are not communicated through any monitoring service
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Health advisories notify you about important but non-critical issues including service retirements and deprecated features, and are communicated at least 90 days in advance, except in urgent cases such as misconfigurations which are reported immediately. A is wrong because service issues concern problems affecting you right now, not planned future changes. C is wrong because Advisor recommends improvements to your configuration rather than announcing Microsoft's product decisions. D is wrong because health advisories exist precisely for this purpose. The storage account and Azure Blueprints retirements covered earlier in this course are exactly this kind of change.

text: What is the difference between metrics and logs in Azure Monitor?
options: Metrics are text records of events; logs are numerical measurements.
Metrics apply to applications; logs apply to infrastructure.
Metrics are numerical measurements collected at intervals; logs are records of events with varying properties.
There is no practical difference; both are stored identically.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Metrics are numerical values describing an aspect of a system at a point in time, suited to dashboards and fast alerting. Logs are records of events, queried with Kusto Query Language. A metric tells you something changed; logs tell you what happened. A is wrong because it reverses the two. B is wrong because both apply to applications and infrastructure alike. D is wrong because they are stored and queried differently, and are suited to different questions.

text: In which language are Log Analytics queries written?
options: SQL
PowerShell
Kusto Query Language
JSON
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Log data in a Log Analytics workspace is queried using Kusto Query Language, usually shortened to KQL. A is wrong, although KQL borrows some familiar ideas from SQL. They are different languages. B is wrong because PowerShell is a management command language, covered in Module 12. It can invoke a query but is not the query language. D is wrong because JSON is a data format used for ARM templates, as covered in Module 12, not a query language.

text: What is a Log Analytics workspace?
options: A dashboard for viewing metrics.
A data store into which log data is collected from Azure and non-Azure resources.
A virtual machine that runs monitoring software.
A region in which monitoring data is processed.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A Log Analytics workspace is a data store into which any type of log data can be collected, from Azure and non-Azure resources and applications alike. It contains tables, and its data is queried with KQL. A is wrong because dashboards are a visualisation feature rather than the data store itself. C is wrong because a workspace is a managed data store, not a machine you operate. D is wrong because a workspace is a resource rather than a geographic concept, although it does reside in a region.

text: A web application is returning errors to users, but the virtual machine hosting it reports normal processor and memory usage. Which Azure Monitor feature is most likely to reveal the problem?
options: Metrics for the virtual machine
Azure Service Health
Azure Advisor
Application Insights
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Application Insights provides application performance monitoring for live applications, tracking request rates, response times, failure rates, exceptions and dependency calls. The scenario describes healthy infrastructure and an unhealthy application, which is exactly the gap it fills. A is wrong, and the scenario says so: the machine's metrics are normal. Infrastructure can be entirely healthy while the application is not. B is wrong because Service Health reports Azure's own issues, and nothing suggests Azure is at fault. C is wrong because Advisor makes configuration recommendations rather than diagnosing a live fault.

text: What is the purpose of an action group in an Azure Monitor alert rule?
options: To define what happens when the alert fires, such as notifications or automated actions.
To group several alerts together for reporting.
To define the condition under which the alert fires.
To assign the alert to a resource group.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. An action group defines the notifications and automated actions triggered when an alert fires, such as sending an email or message, or running a function or webhook. C is wrong because the condition is a separate part of the alert rule. The condition decides whether to fire; the action group decides what then happens. B is wrong because action groups concern responses rather than grouping alerts for reporting. D is wrong because a resource group is a container for resources, covered in Module 5, and is unrelated to alert configuration.

text: According to Microsoft, what do the five Azure Advisor category scores represent?
options: The five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework
The five levels of the Azure hierarchy
The five Azure regions in a geography
The five types of Azure subscription
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Microsoft states that the score for each Advisor category represents one of the five pillars of the Azure Well-Architected Framework: reliability, security, cost optimisation, operational excellence and performance efficiency. B is wrong because the Azure hierarchy has four levels: management group, subscription, resource group and resource, as covered in Module 5. C is wrong because a geography contains two or more regions, and no fixed number of five applies. D is wrong because subscription types are a billing arrangement rather than something Advisor scores.

text: Which statement about Azure Advisor's cost is correct?
options: It is charged per recommendation acted upon.
It requires a paid support plan.
It is charged as a percentage of the savings it identifies.
It is available at no additional cost.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure Advisor is available at no additional cost, and Microsoft describes it as a free personalised guide to Azure best practices. A is wrong because no charge attaches to acting on a recommendation, although implementing one may incur costs for the Azure services involved, such as enabling backup. B is wrong because standard recommendations require no support plan, although some advanced features do require specific support contracts. C is wrong because no such arrangement exists.

text: An organisation wants an automated response, not merely a notification, when a monitored condition occurs. Is this possible with Azure Monitor alerts?
options: No. Alerts can only send notifications.
Only if Azure Advisor is also enabled.
Yes. An action group can trigger automated actions such as running a function or calling a webhook.
Only for security-related conditions.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. An action group can trigger automated actions as well as notifications, including running a function, calling a webhook or creating a support ticket. This is how the enforcement that an Azure budget does not itself provide, as covered in Module 10, is actually built. A is wrong because automated action is one of the main purposes of an action group. B is wrong because Advisor is a separate recommendation service and is not involved in alert automation. D is wrong because automated responses can be configured for any alert condition, not only security ones.

text: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?
options: Authentication establishes who you are; authorisation establishes what you may do.
Authentication establishes what you may do; authorisation establishes who you are.
They are two names for the same process.
Authentication applies to users and authorisation applies to devices.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Authentication proves identity and comes first. Authorisation determines permitted actions and follows. B reverses the two. This reversal is the most common error in this block and costs marks in several places. C is wrong because they are distinct processes performed by different systems. Microsoft Entra ID authenticates; Azure RBAC authorises. D is wrong because both apply to any security principal.

text: Which statement about Microsoft Entra ID is correct?
options: It is the new name for Windows Server Active Directory.
It provides group policy and organisational units in the cloud.
It is a cloud-based identity and access management service, formerly called Azure Active Directory.
It must be installed on domain controllers you maintain.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service, renamed from Azure Active Directory in July 2023. A is an important distinction to get right. Windows Server Active Directory is a separate product that still exists under its own name. B is wrong because group policy and organisational units are Active Directory features. Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides them in Azure; Entra ID does not. D is wrong because it is a cloud service operated by Microsoft.

text: An organisation must move a legacy application to Azure. It requires LDAP and Kerberos authentication and cannot be modified. Which service should it use?
options: Microsoft Entra ID alone
Azure role-based access control
Microsoft Entra External ID
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Domain Services provides managed domain services including LDAP, Kerberos and NTLM authentication, group policy and domain join, without requiring domain controllers to be deployed and patched. A is wrong because Entra ID does not provide LDAP or Kerberos. That is precisely the gap Domain Services fills. B is wrong because RBAC is an authorisation system for Azure resources, not an authentication protocol provider. C is wrong because External ID concerns access for people outside the organisation.

text: Which combination qualifies as multifactor authentication?
options: A password and a security question
A password and a code from an authenticator application on a registered phone
A password and a personal identification number
Two different passwords
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A password is something you know and a registered phone is something you have. Two different categories are required. A is wrong because both a password and a security question are something you know. C is wrong for the same reason. A personal identification number is also something you know. D is the clearest illustration of the rule. Two passwords are two instances of a single factor category.

text: At what point are Conditional Access policies enforced?
options: Before any authentication takes place, as a frontline network defence.
Only when a user attempts to change their password.
After first-factor authentication is completed.
Continuously, replacing the need for authentication.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft states explicitly that Conditional Access policies are enforced after first-factor authentication is completed. A is wrong. Microsoft notes specifically that Conditional Access is not intended as a frontline defence for scenarios such as denial of service attacks. B is wrong because policies apply to access requests generally. D is wrong because Conditional Access follows authentication rather than replacing it.

text: Two Conditional Access policies apply to the same user. One requires multifactor authentication and the other requires a compliant device. What must the user do?
options: Satisfy whichever policy was created first.
Satisfy either one of the two.
Nothing. Conflicting policies cancel each other out.
Satisfy both: complete multifactor authentication and use a compliant device.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Where multiple policies apply, all applicable policies must be satisfied. Assignments are combined with a logical AND. A is wrong because creation order carries no precedence. B is wrong because requirements accumulate rather than offering a choice. C would be a dangerous behaviour if true. The two requirements are not in conflict; both are required.

text: What are the three elements of an Azure RBAC role assignment?
options: Security principal, role definition and scope
Username, password and multifactor authentication
Management group, subscription and resource group
Authentication, authorisation and auditing
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. A role assignment consists of a security principal, meaning who; a role definition, meaning what permissions; and a scope, meaning where those permissions apply. B relates to authentication, which is Entra ID's function rather than RBAC's. C names three of the four scope levels, so it is part of one element rather than all three. D names general security concepts, not the structure of a role assignment.

text: A user is assigned Reader at a management group, and Owner on one subscription inside it. What access does the user have on that subscription?
options: Reader only, because the higher assignment takes precedence.
Contributor, as a compromise between the two.
No access, because the two assignments conflict.
Owner, because permissions are additive.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure role assignments are additive. The user holds the sum of the assignments applying at each scope. A is wrong because a broader assignment does not override a narrower one. Inheritance flows downward and assignments accumulate. B is wrong because Azure does not average or negotiate between roles. C is wrong because the two do not conflict. Additive permissions cannot cancel each other.

text: What are the three guiding principles of Zero Trust?
options: Authenticate, authorise, audit
Verify explicitly, use least privilege access, assume breach
Prevent, detect, respond
Confidentiality, integrity, availability
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. These are the three principles as Microsoft states them. A names general access management stages rather than the Zero Trust principles. C describes a security operations lifecycle. D names the three properties of the classic security triad, which is a different framework.

text: Which statement correctly describes the two core components of Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
options: Authentication and authorisation
Single sign-on and multifactor authentication
Cloud security posture management, which assesses configuration, and cloud workload protection, which defends running workloads from threats
Foundational and advanced, which differ only in price
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Posture management continuously assesses resources against security standards and issues recommendations; workload protection defends workloads from threats. The first prevents problems, the second detects attacks. A names identity processes handled by Entra ID and Azure RBAC. B names authentication methods. D is wrong because although foundational posture management is free and other plans are paid, price is not what distinguishes the two core components.

text: An organisation notices the same virtual machine size costs different amounts in two Azure regions. Which cost factor explains this?
options: Geography
Consumption
Resource type
Subscription type
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. The same service can cost different amounts in different regions, because the underlying costs of power, land and connectivity differ. B is wrong because consumption concerns how much of a service is used, not where it runs. C is wrong because the resource type is identical in both cases. D is wrong because the subscription type sets the baseline rate across the account.

text: Which statement about network traffic costs in Azure is correct?
options: Both data entering and data leaving Azure are billed at the same rate.
Data entering Azure is generally free; data leaving a region or leaving Azure is generally billed.
All network traffic within Azure is free.
Data leaving Azure is free; data entering is billed.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The asymmetry is the point to remember. Ingress is generally not billed; egress generally is. A is wrong because the two directions are treated differently. C is wrong because traffic leaving a region is generally billed even when it remains within Azure. D reverses the arrangement, which is a common distractor.

text: Which tool would you use to estimate the cost of a proposed Azure deployment before creating any resources?
options: Microsoft Cost Management
Azure Advisor
The Azure pricing calculator
Azure Monitor
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. The pricing calculator turns anticipated usage into an estimated cost, which is a planning task performed before deployment. A is wrong because Cost Management reports actual consumption. With nothing deployed there is no consumption data. B is wrong because Advisor analyses resources that already exist. D is wrong because Azure Monitor concerns operational telemetry rather than cost estimation.

text: Which statement about the Total Cost of Ownership calculator is currently accurate?
options: It has been deprecated by Microsoft and no longer appears in the current AZ-900 objectives.
It is the recommended tool for estimating Azure service costs before deployment.
It has been renamed the Azure pricing calculator.
It is a feature within Microsoft Cost Management.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Microsoft has deprecated the Total Cost of Ownership calculator, and the current exam objective names only the pricing calculator. Much preparation material still covers both. B describes the pricing calculator. The TCO calculator estimated migration savings, which is a different question. C is wrong because they were two separate tools answering different questions. D is wrong because it was a standalone web tool.

text: A budget of a set amount is created for a subscription. Spending reaches that amount. What happens?
options: Azure stops all resources in the subscription automatically.
An alert is raised, and spending continues.
Azure prevents new resources from being created.
The subscription is disabled until the next billing period.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. A budget in Azure is a monitoring and alerting mechanism. It notifies when actual or forecast spending approaches or exceeds the threshold, but does not itself stop anything. A is the most dangerous misconception in this topic because it produces false confidence. Automated shutdown is possible, but it must be built by connecting an alert to an automation. C is wrong for the same reason. D is wrong because reaching a budget threshold has no effect on the subscription's status.

text: A tag is applied to a resource group. What happens to the resources inside it?
options: They inherit the tag automatically.
They inherit the tag after the next billing cycle.
They do not inherit the tag. Each resource carries only tags applied to it directly.
They inherit the tag only if created after the tag was applied.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Tags are not inherited from a resource group to the resources inside it, nor from a subscription to its resource groups. A is the most commonly held misconception about tags, and believing it is how organisations end up with most spending showing as untagged. B is wrong because billing cycles have no effect on tag inheritance. D is wrong because creation order makes no difference. Inheritance requires Azure Policy.

text: To which of the following can tags be applied?
options: Management groups only
Resources only
All levels of the Azure hierarchy including management groups
Resources, resource groups and subscriptions, but not management groups
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Tags can be applied to Azure resources, resource groups and subscriptions. Management groups are the exception and cannot be tagged. A reverses the actual position exactly. B is wrong because resource groups and subscriptions can also be tagged. C is wrong because of the management group exception, which is the examinable detail here.

text: An organisation must ensure that resources can only be deployed to South Africa North. Which service enforces this?
options: Azure role-based access control
A resource lock
Azure Policy
Microsoft Purview
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Ensuring resources are deployed only to allowed regions is one of Microsoft's own stated examples of what Azure Policy enforces. The requirement names a resource property, which is the signal for Policy. A is wrong because role-based access control governs who may perform actions, not what resources may look like. B is wrong because a lock prevents deletion or modification of existing resources. D is wrong because Purview governs the data estate.

text: What is the essential difference between Azure Policy and Azure role-based access control?
options: Role-based access control governs who may perform actions; Policy governs what resources may look like.
They are two names for the same mechanism.
Policy applies to users; role-based access control applies to resources.
Policy applies only to management groups; role-based access control only to resources.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Role-based access control concerns identities and their permissions. Azure Policy concerns resource properties and configuration. They are complementary. B is wrong because they govern entirely different things. C reverses the two exactly. D is wrong because both can be applied across the hierarchy.

text: A lock of type CanNotDelete is applied to a virtual machine. What can an authorised user still do?
options: Nothing. The resource is completely frozen.
Read and modify the resource, but not delete it.
Read the resource only.
Delete the resource, but not modify it.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. CanNotDelete means authorised users can read and modify a resource, but they cannot delete it. A is wrong because modification remains permitted. C describes the effect of a ReadOnly lock, which is the other lock type. D reverses the behaviour. Deletion is precisely what this lock prevents.

text: A subscription Owner attempts to delete a resource protected by a CanNotDelete lock. What happens?
options: The deletion succeeds, because Owner is the highest role.
The deletion succeeds but generates a compliance warning.
The deletion is queued until the lock expires.
The deletion is blocked. The lock overrides user permissions and must be removed first.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. A lock overrides any user permissions. Unlike role-based access control, a management lock applies a restriction across all users and all roles. A is the misconception the question exists to correct. No role bypasses a lock. B is wrong because the operation is blocked outright. C is wrong because locks do not expire. They persist until deliberately removed.

text: Which statement about the scope of resource locks is correct?
options: Locks apply to both control plane and data plane operations.
Locks apply only to data plane operations.
Locks apply only to control plane operations, so they protect the resource but not the data inside it.
Locks apply only to resources created after the lock was set.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. A CanNotDelete lock on a storage account prevents the account being deleted, but does not prevent blobs inside it being deleted, because that is a data plane operation. A is wrong, and believing it produces a dangerous false confidence about data protection. B reverses the position exactly. D is wrong because a lock applied at a parent scope is inherited by resources added later.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, what are the two primary data governance solutions in Microsoft Purview?
options: Data Map, Data Catalog and Data Estate Insights
Data Map and Unified Catalog
Azure Policy and resource locks
Compliance Manager and Secure Score
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Microsoft's current documentation names Data Map, which scans sources to capture metadata, and Unified Catalog, the searchable catalogue where data is curated. A describes an earlier structure and appears in a great deal of AZ-900 material published recently. C names Azure resource governance mechanisms, not Purview solutions. D relates to compliance and security scoring.

text: A data steward is granted a role in Microsoft Purview Unified Catalog. What access does this give them to the underlying data?
options: Full read access to all catalogued data.
Read access, but only to data classified as non-sensitive.
Access determined by the sensitivity labels applied.
None. Purview holds metadata, and its roles do not provide access to the underlying data.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Microsoft states explicitly that all data in Data Map and Unified Catalog is metadata rather than the underlying data, and that no role in either provides access to the underlying data itself. A is the assumption that makes this a worthwhile question. Purview is a catalogue, not a copy. B and C are both wrong for the same reason. No level of access to underlying data is granted by a Purview role.

text: Which statement best describes the relationship between Azure Cloud Shell, Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell?
options: Cloud Shell is a browser-based terminal in which either Azure CLI or Azure PowerShell can be used.
They are three alternative tools that do different jobs.
Cloud Shell replaced Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell.
Azure CLI runs on Linux and Azure PowerShell on Windows, and Cloud Shell on neither.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Cloud Shell is a place: an interactive, authenticated, browser-accessible terminal offering a choice of Bash or PowerShell. The command line interface and Azure PowerShell are the command sets used within it. B is wrong because the command line interface and PowerShell do the same job in different syntax. C is wrong because both remain current and can also be installed locally. D is wrong because both tools are cross-platform.

text: After how long without interactive activity does a Cloud Shell session time out?
options: 5 minutes
60 minutes
It does not time out
20 minutes
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. A Cloud Shell session times out after 20 minutes without interactive activity. A is wrong, although 5 GB is the size of the file share used when storage is attached, which is where the number 5 comes from in this topic. B is wrong because the timeout is considerably shorter than an hour. C is wrong because Cloud Shell runs on a temporary host provided per session.

text: According to Microsoft's current documentation, does Azure Cloud Shell require a storage account?
options: Yes, always. Cloud Shell cannot start without one.
Yes, but only when using PowerShell mode.
No. An ephemeral session can be started without storage, but files do not persist.
No, and files persist regardless.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Microsoft's current documentation states that when starting Cloud Shell you have the option of using it with or without an attached storage account. Continuing without storage is called an ephemeral session. A is what almost every AZ-900 guide still says, and it reflects the older arrangement. B is wrong because the choice does not depend on which shell is selected. D is wrong because persistence is exactly what an ephemeral session does not provide.

text: An organisation wants to manage Windows and Linux servers running in its own datacentre using Azure tools, without moving them to Azure. Which service enables this?
options: Azure Resource Manager
Azure Migrate
Azure Cloud Shell
Azure Arc
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Azure Arc projects existing non-Azure and on-premises resources into Azure Resource Manager, so they can be managed with Azure tools while continuing to run where they are. A is wrong because Resource Manager is the management service that Arc projects resources into. B is wrong because Azure Migrate discovers, assesses and migrates workloads. Migration is precisely what this organisation does not want. C is wrong because Cloud Shell is a terminal for running commands.

text: Which of the following best describes infrastructure as code?
options: Writing application code that runs on cloud infrastructure.
Defining infrastructure in files that can be version-controlled, reviewed and deployed repeatedly.
Using a graphical interface to configure infrastructure more quickly.
Installing code libraries onto virtual machines automatically.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Infrastructure as code means defining the infrastructure in code, storing it in a source repository and versioning it, so anyone on the team can deploy a consistent environment. A describes ordinary application development. C is wrong because a graphical interface is the alternative to infrastructure as code, not a form of it. D describes configuration management rather than defining the infrastructure.

text: An ARM template is deployed. The same template is then deployed again without any changes. What happens?
options: The deployment fails, because the resources already exist.
Duplicate resources are created.
The existing resources are deleted and recreated.
The deployment succeeds and the resources remain in the same state, because templates are idempotent.
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Microsoft states that templates are idempotent, meaning you can deploy the same template many times and get the same resource types in the same state. A describes what a naive imperative script would typically do. B is wrong because the template names the resources, so redeploying refers to the same ones. C is wrong because Resource Manager does not destroy and recreate resources that already match the desired state.

text: What is Azure Resource Manager?
options: A tool for writing ARM templates.
The deployment and management service through which every request to create, update or delete an Azure resource passes.
A monitoring service for Azure resources.
The graphical interface used to manage Azure.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. The portal, the command line interface, PowerShell, the interfaces and templates are all clients of Resource Manager, which is why they produce identical results. A is wrong because templates are written in an editor. Resource Manager receives and acts on them. C is wrong because monitoring is provided by Azure Monitor. D describes the Azure portal, which is one of several clients of Resource Manager.

text: Which service analyses your resource configuration and usage, then recommends improvements?
options: Azure Advisor
Azure Service Health
Azure Monitor
Microsoft Purview
explanation: Correct Answer: A. A is correct. Azure Advisor analyses resource configuration and usage telemetry and recommends solutions, which is why Microsoft describes it as a personalised cloud consultant. B is wrong because Service Health reports issues with Azure itself rather than with your configuration. C is wrong because Azure Monitor collects and analyses telemetry about what your resources are doing. D is wrong because Microsoft Purview governs the data estate.

text: Which of the following is one of Azure Advisor's five recommendation categories?
options: Compliance
Governance
Operational excellence
Availability zones
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. The five categories are reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence. A is wrong because compliance is not an Advisor category. B is wrong because governance is a separate topic rather than an Advisor category. D is wrong because availability zones are a resilience mechanism, not a recommendation category.

text: A widespread Azure outage is affecting many customers globally. Which component reports this publicly, without requiring sign-in?
options: Resource Health
Service Health
Azure Status
Azure Monitor
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Azure Status is a public page reporting Azure issues with widespread impact, visible to anyone without signing in. A is wrong because Resource Health reports the health of your individual resources. B is wrong because Service Health is personalised to your subscriptions and requires sign-in. D is wrong because Azure Monitor reports on your own resources rather than Azure's service status.

text: Microsoft is retiring a service the organisation depends on. Where is this communicated, and how far in advance?
options: As a service issue, communicated when the retirement occurs
As a health advisory, communicated at least 90 days in advance
As an Advisor recommendation, communicated immediately
Retirements are not communicated through any monitoring service
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. Health advisories notify you about important but non-critical issues including service retirements, and are communicated at least 90 days in advance, except in urgent cases such as misconfigurations. A is wrong because service issues concern problems affecting you right now, not planned future changes. C is wrong because Advisor recommends improvements to your configuration rather than announcing product decisions. D is wrong because health advisories exist precisely for this purpose.

text: What is the difference between metrics and logs in Azure Monitor?
options: Metrics are text records of events; logs are numerical measurements.
Metrics apply to applications; logs apply to infrastructure.
Metrics are numerical measurements collected at intervals; logs are records of events with varying properties.
There is no practical difference; both are stored identically.
explanation: Correct Answer: C. C is correct. Metrics are numerical values describing an aspect of a system at a point in time. Logs are records of events, queried with Kusto Query Language. A metric tells you something changed; logs tell you what happened. A reverses the two. B is wrong because both apply to applications and infrastructure alike. D is wrong because they are stored and queried differently.

text: A web application is returning errors to users, but the virtual machine hosting it reports normal processor and memory usage. Which Azure Monitor feature is most likely to reveal the problem?
options: Metrics for the virtual machine
Azure Service Health
Azure Advisor
Application Insights
explanation: Correct Answer: D. D is correct. Application Insights provides application performance monitoring for live applications, tracking request rates, response times, failure rates, exceptions and dependency calls. The scenario describes healthy infrastructure and an unhealthy application. A is wrong, and the scenario says so: the machine's metrics are normal. B is wrong because nothing suggests Azure is at fault. C is wrong because Advisor makes configuration recommendations rather than diagnosing a live fault.

text: An organisation wants an automated response, not merely a notification, when a monitored condition occurs. Is this possible with Azure Monitor alerts?
options: No. Alerts can only send notifications.
Yes. An action group can trigger automated actions such as running a function or calling a webhook.
Only if Azure Advisor is also enabled.
Only for security-related conditions.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. B is correct. An action group can trigger automated actions as well as notifications, including running a function, calling a webhook or creating a support ticket. This is how the enforcement that an Azure budget does not itself provide is actually built. A is wrong because automated action is one of the main purposes of an action group. C is wrong because Advisor is a separate recommendation service. D is wrong because automated responses can be configured for any alert condition.
